target_customer: Retail buyers and sellers of bullion and certified rare coins, plus dealers
problem: Retailers charge 10 to 30 percent over spot on precious metals while cash-for-gold buyers pay about 30 percent under spot; no transparent price discovery exists.
business_model: marketplace take rate on an order book
product_category: precious metals and rare coin marketplace

founders.name: Trey Benedict
previous_startups: Collect Pure: Scan Rare Coins app
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a numismatist.

founders.name: David Gordillo
founders.background_notes: Presented the YC launch post with Benedict, which says they met working on sneaker botting projects (via a company blog seen in search); the YC company page does not list him.

technical_complexity.rationale: Order book marketplace with authenticated inventory; logistics and vaulting partnerships are the hard part, not the software.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided liquidity could compound, but large dealers and eBay can list the same goods.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large online dealers existed; no source shows them copying the order book model.

market_need_then: The YC launch post cites predatory premiums and 30 percent below spot buyback; the company claims an 11B rare coin and 55B precious metals market.

branding.domain_note: Brand is Pure but domain is collectpure.com, inherited from the earlier Collect Pure coin scanning app.

identity.logo: black and white wordmark, green app banner artwork

branding.community_and_virality: Third party coin blogs and a founder podcast appearance cover the marketplace; Trustpilot rating 4.5 per site.

brand_strength.rationale: Short evocative name conveying purity and authenticity, helped by trust messaging, but generic with domain compromise.

pivots.to: Pure marketplace for bullion and rare coins
pivots.why: Per a company blog seen in search results, founders always wanted a StockX like marketplace; date not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Pure is active, grew from the YC launch to an order book marketplace with sellers, vaulting and a Trustpilot presence, and its team size is the largest of those in this batch of records. No acquisition, shutdown or lawsuit was found. A reported November 2025 round of about 15.6M is on aggregators only, so financing success is plausible but unverified.
notes: VCBacked lists 15.6M, Series Unknown, November 2025, investors Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund; CB Insights snippets say 15.55M on 2025-11-04 (one page calling it Series A); FundedIQ says 31.1M across 2 rounds. These are aggregators only and conflict, so no round recorded and funding_data_coverage is none_found. A second search found no announcement. The launch post says 'over 3 years ago' with no exact date. Competition: no dated 2022 competitor source found; APMEX and JM Bullion appear only in 2025 and 2026 listicles.
